isomorphic_questions.stem: A dolphin leaps out of the water with a speed of 12 m/s at an angle 𝜑. What is the speed of the dolphin when it is at its maximum height?

options.explanation: At maximum height, the vertical component of velocity is zero, while the horizontal component remains constant.
Correct. The horizontal component of the velocity, $v_{x} = v \cos \phi$, remains the same throughout the motion.
This represents the initial vertical component, which becomes zero at maximum height.
The horizontal component of velocity is not zero at the maximum height.

isomorphic_questions.stem: A rover is moving on a flat surface with an initial velocity of \( \mathbf{v} = (15.5\, \text{m/s}) \hat{i} \) when its thrusters produce an acceleration of \( \mathbf{a} = (3.0\, \text{m/s}^2) \hat{i} + (1.5\, \text{m/s}^2) \hat{j} \). Based on this scenario, which statement is true?

options.text: The x-component of the rover’s velocity stays the same.
options.explanation: The x-velocity changes due to the i-direction acceleration.

options.text: The y-component of the rover’s velocity stays the same.
options.explanation: The y-velocity changes due to the j-direction acceleration.

options.text: Both the speed and direction change.
options.explanation: Correct. Both the x and y components of velocity change, affecting the speed and direction.

options.text: None of the statements above are correct.
options.explanation: This is incorrect as option C accurately describes the situation.
